title: Daily, Weekly & Fortnightly Driving Limits
whatItIs: Under the assimilated rules: no more than 9 hours of driving a day (10 hours twice in a fixed week), 56 hours in a fixed week and 90 hours in any two consecutive weeks.

keyFacts.text: Daily driving MUST NOT exceed 9 hours. It can go up to 10 hours, but only twice in a fixed week.

keyFacts: Daily driving time is all the driving between the end of one daily rest and the start of the next.

keyFacts.text: Weekly driving MUST NOT exceed 56 hours in a fixed week.

keyFacts: A fixed week runs from 00.00 on Monday to 24.00 on the following Sunday.

keyFacts.text: Driving in any two consecutive weeks MUST NOT exceed 90 hours.

keyFacts: Example of a full week: 4 days of 9 hours + 2 days of 10 hours = 56 hours.

a.label: 56 hours
points: Most driving in one fixed week

b.label: 90 hours
points: Most driving in any two consecutive weeks
So two 56-hour weeks in a row would break the limit

onTheTest.question: You drove for 56 hours last week. Under the assimilated rules, what is the most you can drive this week?
onTheTest.why: Driving in any two consecutive weeks must not exceed 90 hours, so 90 − 56 = 34 hours this week.

onTheTest.question: How many times in a fixed week can you extend your daily driving time to 10 hours?
onTheTest.why: The maximum daily driving time is 9 hours. It can be increased to 10 hours twice in a fixed week.

traps: 10-hour days: twice in a fixed week, not twice between weekly rests.
Two 56-hour weeks in a row break the 90-hour two-week limit.
Off-road driving between rests counts towards the daily limit if you also drove on public roads.
